reconstruction.title: SupaJuce 1 — two-square oscillator octave check
reconstruction.method: Hardware-only FFT/STFT inspection of the first phrase. Lower square fundamentals near 330, 220, 294 and 196 Hz identify sounding MIDI 64, 57, 62 and 55. Undo the published Upper tone octave shift -1 to infer played MIDI 76, 69, 74 and 67. Strong even-numbered families at twice those frequencies, including H6 but not H4, identify the second square one octave above; this is consistent with published OSC1 coarse raw 100/WIDE off and OSC2 raw 64/WIDE off. Onsets and gates estimated from spectral renewals; no synthesis parameter fitting.
uncertainties: Original MIDI is unavailable; this is an estimated reconstruction.
Event boundaries are approximate within 10–20 ms; pitch envelope, filter release and delay obscure exact key-down/up times.
All velocities are placeholders at 100. Original velocity, controllers, system transpose, recording processing and exact patch revision are unverified.
Lower square note identification is stronger than exact gates. The first 1.8 seconds exclude the rest of the demo and use an artificial final crop.

interpretation: The hardware contains the odd-harmonic family of a square at twice the lower square frequency (H2,H6,H10,H14) while H4,H8,H12 are suppressed. The correction moves OSC1 from eight times OSC2 frequency to twice it. Upper carrier level and higher harmonic balance still differ from hardware.
limitations: Frequencies refine supplied hardware-only pitch hypotheses within +/-1.5%; the lowest nonzero harmonic and second-square family jointly support the octave inference.
Played-note inference assumes published Upper tone OCTAVE -1 and unchanged system tuning. Original notes, velocity, gates, controllers and exact recorded patch revision are unknown.
Delay and reverb are enabled. Later note windows contain earlier notes or tails; their harmonic-fit residuals are retained. The first window is the strongest isolated check.
Centroid closeness alone is misleading: before was closer in centroid despite placing the dominant oscillator in the wrong harmonic family.
This endpoint recording supports raw100/WIDEoff at +12 relative semitones. It does not calibrate intermediate raw values or WIDE-on behavior.
